components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main action: Search, Book a seat, Post a ride.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); border: none; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 16px; font: 500 14px 'Figtree Variable', sans-serif; transition: background .15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action: Show on map, Edit.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 16px; font: 500 14px 'Figtree Variable', sans-serif; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--muted); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

narrative.overview: Pool is built around the trip, not the app. Every screen answers the same questions a rider or driver asks before leaving: when does it go, from where to where, how many seats are left, and what does it cost. Those facts are set large and bold; everything else steps back. One warm terracotta carries the brand, the way a single brand colour carries Rapido or Zomato, so the interface feels like a friendly consumer app rather than an admin template.
keyCharacteristics: One brand colour (terracotta) for actions, selection, active navigation and brand tints.
Trip facts (departure time, fare) in extra-bold, tabular figures.
White rounded cards on a soft grey ground, separated by shadow instead of borders.
Figtree throughout, from page titles to labels.
Not themed: no tickets, signs or codes used as decoration.

rules.name: The One Colour Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is the only brand hue. Status colours appear only inside status badges, where they carry meaning.

rules.name: The Readable Terracotta Rule
rules.body: Light theme puts white text on terracotta; dark theme puts dark text on bright terracotta. Never lighten terracotta while keeping white text on it.

rules.name: The Trip Facts Rule
rules.body: Departure time and fare are always the largest, boldest text on a ride card, in tabular figures.

rules.name: The No Box-in-Box Rule
rules.body: A card never sits inside another card, and card footers have no grey strip or divider.

dos: Do use terracotta only for actions, selection, active navigation and brand tints.
Do set departure times and fares in extra-bold tabular figures (DepartureTime, text-2xl font-extrabold).
Do lift cards with the card-lift shadow on the road-grey ground.
Do keep every new colour inside the theme tokens in src/index.css and every badge in badges.tsx.
donts: Don't add decorative themes (tickets, road signs, codes, dot patterns) to working screens.
Don't put grey footer strips, divider lines or nested cards inside cards.
Don't use heavy gradients, glow or animation everywhere; the user rejected "too flashy".
Don't put white text on a lighter terracotta than terracotta.
Don't add a small label above a heading; the heading carries itself.
